text:
Mikko Rantanen had his best night of the month on Tuesday in Vegas: a goal, three assists and five shots in 24 minutes as Dallas came back from two down to win in overtime, including a dance around a defender at the blue line to set up Lundkvist that Jesse Granger called a heck of a play. It fits the season. He has 26 points in 21 games, 12 on the power play, and Dallas takes 56% of the expected goals at five on five with him on.

Some of it is running hot. Ten goals on 6.1 expected means 24% shooting against 16% last year, and his team has scored 6.1 more goals than expected with him on the ice. His own shot volume is down (0.86 expected goals per 60 after 1.02), and his ice time over the last 10 has dipped to 19:55.

Our range has his true rate close to what he's producing anyway, and a full season around 95 points. He still carries the puck in on most entries, 56% last season in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. The assists are the steady part; the goals will slow.
